title.zh: 卷八十三 列傳第十三: 耶律休哥 耶律斜軫 耶律奚低 耶律學古
title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 13: Yelu Xiuge, Yelu Xiezhen, Yelu Xidi, Yelu Xuegu
title.raw: 卷八十三 列傳第十三: 耶律休哥 耶律斜軫 耶律奚低 耶律學古 Volume 83 Biographies 13: Yelu Xiuge, Yelu Xiezhen, Yelu Xidi, Yelu Xuegu

sentences.zh: 耶律休哥

translations.literal: Yelu Xiuge
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiuge

sentences.zh: 耶律休哥，字遜寧。

translations.literal: Yelu Xiuge, courtesy name Xunning.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiuge, whose courtesy name was Xunning.

sentences.zh: 祖釋魯，隋國王。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Shilu, King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shilu had been King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 父綰思，南院夷離堇。

translations.literal: His father was Wansi, Yilibi of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wansi had served as Yilibi of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 休哥少有公輔器。

translations.literal: Xiuge in youth had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Even in youth Xiuge showed the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初烏古、室韋二部叛，休哥從北府宰相蕭幹討之。

translations.literal: At first the two tribes Ugu and Shiwei rebelled; Xiuge followed the Northern Court chancellor Xiao Gan to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ugu and Shiwei tribes first rebelled, Xiuge accompanied Northern Court Chancellor Xiao Gan to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 應歷末，為惕隱。

translations.literal: At the end of Yingli, he became Tiyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yingli reign he was made Tiyi.

sentences.zh: 乾亨元年，宋侵燕，北院大王奚底、統軍使蕭討古等敗績，南京被圍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianheng, Song invaded Yan; the Northern Court great king Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others were defeated, and the Southern Capital was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianheng, when Song invaded Yan, the Northern Court Great King Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others suffered defeat and the Southern Capital came under siege.

sentences.zh: 帝命休哥代奚底，將五院軍往救。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiuge to replace Xidi and lead the Five Corps armies to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xiuge to replace Xidi and march to the relief with the armies of the Five Corps.

sentences.zh: 遇大敵於高梁河，與耶律斜軫分左右翼，擊敗之。

translations.literal: He met the main enemy force at the Gaoliang River; with Yelu Xiezhen he took left and right wings and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Gaoliang River he met the main enemy force; he and Yelu Xiezhen took the left and right wings and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 追殺三十餘里，斬首萬餘級，休哥被三創。

translations.literal: Pursuit and slaughter extended more than thirty li; over ten thousand heads were taken; Xiuge received three wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than thirty li, and heads numbered above ten thousand; Xiuge himself took three wounds.

sentences.zh: 明旦，宋主遁去，休哥以創不能騎，輕車追至涿州，不及而還。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the Song emperor fled; Xiuge, unable to ride because of his wounds, pursued in a light cart to Zhuozhou but failed to overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Song ruler fled. Too badly wounded to ride, Xiuge pursued in a light cart as far as Zhuozhou but could not catch up and turned back.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，上命韓匡嗣、耶律沙伐宋，以報圍城之役。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor ordered Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha to attack Song in reprisal for the siege.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor sent Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha against Song to repay the siege.

sentences.zh: 休哥率本部兵從匡嗣等戰於滿城。

translations.literal: Xiuge led his own troops to follow Kuangsi and the others in battle at Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge led his own troops to join Kuangsi and fought at Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 翌日將復戰，宋人請降，匡嗣信之。

translations.literal: The next day, as battle was to be resumed, the Song troops asked to surrender and Kuangsi believed them.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was to resume the next day, the Song troops offered surrender and Kuangsi believed them.

sentences.zh: 休哥曰：「彼眾整而銳，必不肯屈，乃誘我耳。

translations.literal: Xiuge said: "Their force is ordered and keen; they will surely not submit—this is only to lure us.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge said, "Their ranks are tight and their troops are keen—they will never truly yield; this is a ruse.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴兵以待。」

translations.literal: We ought to hold the army in strict readiness and await them."
translations.idiomatic: We should keep the army under strict guard and wait."

sentences.zh: 匡嗣不聽。

translations.literal: Kuangsi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 休哥引兵憑高而視。

translations.literal: Xiuge drew up his troops on high ground to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge drew his men up on high ground to watch.

sentences.zh: 須臾南兵大至，鼓噪疾馳。

translations.literal: In a moment the southern troops arrived in force, shouting and galloping hard.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the southern army arrived in force, beating drums and charging at full speed.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣倉卒不知所為，士卒棄旗鼓而走，遂敗績。

translations.literal: Kuangsi in haste knew not what to do; soldiers cast aside flags and drums and fled; thus defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi, caught off guard, did not know what to do; his men threw down flags and drums and fled, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 休哥整兵進擊，敵乃卻。

translations.literal: Xiuge reformed his troops and pressed the attack; the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge reformed his lines and pressed forward, and only then did the enemy fall back.

sentences.zh: 詔總南面戍兵，為北院大王。

translations.literal: He was ordered to take overall command of the southern garrison troops and was made Great King of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take command of all southern garrison troops and was made Great King of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 明年，車駕親征，圍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in person and besieged Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor led a personal campaign and laid siege to Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來救，守將張師突圍出。

translations.literal: Song troops came to the relief; the defending general Zhang Shi broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops marched to relieve the pass, and the defending general Zhang Shi broke out through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 帝親督戰，休哥斬師，餘眾退走入城。

translations.literal: The emperor personally supervised the battle; Xiuge slew Shi, and the rest retreated into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally directed the battle; Xiuge killed Zhang Shi, and the survivors fled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 宋陣於水南。

translations.literal: The Song army formed battle lines south of the water.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army drew up south of the river.

sentences.zh: 將戰，帝以休哥馬介獨黃，慮為敵所識，乃賜玄甲、白馬易之。

translations.literal: Before the fight, because Xiuge's horse had a saddle cloth of distinctive yellow and he feared the enemy would know him, the emperor bestowed dark armor and a white horse in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle the emperor saw that Xiuge's horse wore a distinctive yellow saddle cloth that might mark him to the enemy, so he gave him black armor and a white horse in exchange.

sentences.zh: 休哥率精騎渡水，擊敗之，追至莫州。

translations.literal: Xiuge led picked cavalry across the water, defeated them, and pursued to Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge led crack cavalry across the river, routed them, and pursued as far as Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 橫屍滿道，靫矢俱罄，生獲數將以獻。

translations.literal: Corpses lay across the road; quivers and arrows were all spent; several generals were captured alive and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses choked the roads; quivers were empty of arrows; several generals were taken alive and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜御馬、金盂，勞之曰：「爾勇過於名，若人人如卿，何憂不克？」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed his own horse and a golden bowl, encouraging him and saying: "Your courage surpasses your fame; if every man were like you, what worry would there be of not conquering?"
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor gave him an imperial horse and a golden bowl and praised him: "Your courage outstrips your fame. If every man were like you, how could we fail to prevail?"

sentences.zh: 師還，拜於越。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 聖宗即位，太后稱制，令休哥總南面軍務，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shengzong took the throne, the empress dowager held regency and ordered Xiuge to take overall southern military affairs with discretion to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shengzong ascended the throne and the empress dowager assumed regency, Xiuge was placed in overall charge of southern military affairs with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 休哥均戍兵，立更休法，勸農桑，修武備，邊境大治。

translations.literal: Xiuge equalized garrison troops, established rotation and rest regulations, encouraged farming and sericulture, repaired armaments, and the frontier was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge equalized the garrisons, instituted rotation and rest for the troops, promoted farming and sericulture, and strengthened defenses until the borderlands were thoroughly settled.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，宋復來侵，其將範密、楊繼業出雲州；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, Song again invaded; its generals Fan Mi and Yang Ye came out from Yunzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe the Song invaded again: Fan Mi and Yang Ye advanced from Yunzhou;

sentences.zh: 曹彬、米信出雄、易，取歧溝、涿州，陷固安，置屯。

translations.literal: Cao Bin and Mi Xin came out from Xiong and Yi, took Qigou and Zhuozhou, captured Gu'an, and set up camps.
translations.idiomatic: while Cao Bin and Mi Xin marched from Xiong and Yi, seized Qigou and Zhuozhou, took Gu'an, and entrenched.

sentences.zh: 時北南院、奚部兵未至，休哥力寡，不敢出戰。

translations.literal: At that time the troops of the Northern and Southern Courts and the Xi tribes had not yet arrived; Xiuge's force was few and he dared not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of the Northern and Southern Courts and the Xi tribes had not yet arrived, and with his small force Xiuge did not dare to offer battle.

sentences.zh: 夜以輕騎出兩軍間，殺其單弱以脅餘眾；

translations.literal: By night he sent light cavalry out between the two armies, killing their isolated and weak to intimidate the rest;
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent light cavalry between the enemy armies to cut down stragglers and isolated parties and intimidate the rest;

sentences.zh: 晝則以精銳張其勢，使彼勞於防禦，以疲其力。

translations.literal: by day he displayed elite troops to magnify his force and make them weary at defense to exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: by day he paraded elite troops to inflate his apparent strength and wear them down with constant defense.

sentences.zh: 又設伏林莽，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: He also set ambushes in woods and thickets and cut their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: He laid ambushes in the woods as well and severed their supply lines.

sentences.zh: 曹彬等以糧運不繼，退保白溝。

translations.literal: Cao Bin and the others, because grain transport did not continue, withdrew to defend Baigou.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies failed, Cao Bin and his colleagues fell back to Baigou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，復至。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month, they came again.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month they returned.

sentences.zh: 休哥以輕兵薄之，伺彼蓐食，擊其離伍單出者，且戰且卻。

translations.literal: Xiuge pressed them with light troops, watching for when they took mat rations, striking those who left formation alone, fighting while withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge harassed them with light troops, striking men who left the ranks alone at mealtimes, fighting and giving ground by turns.

sentences.zh: 由是南軍自救不暇，結方陣，塹地兩邊而行。

translations.literal: Thereby the southern army had no leisure even to save themselves; they formed square arrays and dug ditches on both sides as they marched.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army could barely defend itself; they formed squares and dug trenches on both flanks as they advanced.

sentences.zh: 軍渴乏井，漉淖而飲，凡四日始達於涿。

translations.literal: The army thirsted and wells were scarce; they strained mud and drank; only after four days did they reach Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Thirsty and short of wells, they strained muddy water to drink, and only after four days did they reach Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 聞太后軍至，彬等冒雨而遁。

translations.literal: Hearing the empress dowager's army had arrived, Bin and the others fled through rain.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard the empress dowager's army was coming, Bin and his commanders fled through the rain.

sentences.zh: 太后益以銳卒，追及之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager added crack troops and overtook them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager reinforced the pursuit with crack troops and overtook them.

sentences.zh: 彼力窮，環糧車自衛，休哥圍之。

translations.literal: Their strength was spent; they ringed grain wagons to defend themselves; Xiuge besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: With their strength spent, they circled their grain wagons for protection; Xiuge surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 至夜，彬、信以數騎亡去，餘眾悉潰。

translations.literal: By night Bin and Xin escaped with several horsemen; the rest all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: By night Cao Bin and Mi Xin slipped away with a few horsemen while the rest broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 追至易州東，聞宋師尚有數萬，瀕沙河而爨，促兵往擊之。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached east of Yizhou; hearing the Song army still numbered tens of thousands cooking along the Sha River, he urged troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached east of Yizhou, where he learned that tens of thousands of Song troops were cooking along the Sha River; he pressed his men to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 宋師望塵奔竄，墮岸相蹂死者過半，沙河為之不流。

translations.literal: The Song army fled at the sight of dust; more than half died falling from banks and trampling one another; the Sha River ceased to flow for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army fled at the first dust of the pursuit; more than half perished tumbling from the banks or trampling one another, and the Sha River was dammed with the dead.

sentences.zh: 太后旋旆，休哥收宋屍為京觀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager turned her banners home; Xiuge gathered Song corpses into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress dowager turned homeward, Xiuge heaped the Song dead into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 封宋國王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.

sentences.zh: 又上言，可乘宋弱，略地至河為界。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying that while Song was weak, territory might be taken with the river as border.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that with Song weakened, they could seize territory as far as the river for a new border.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was presented and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 及太后南征，休哥為先鋒，敗宋兵於望都。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager campaigned south, Xiuge was vanguard and defeated Song troops at Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's southern campaign, Xiuge served as vanguard and defeated the Song at Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 時宋將劉廷讓以數萬騎並海而出，約與李敬源合兵，聲言取燕。

translations.literal: At that time the Song general Liu Tingrang led tens of thousands of cavalry along the coast, agreeing to join forces with Li Jingyuan, proclaiming the taking of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Liu Tingrang then led tens of thousands of cavalry along the coast, intending to join Li Jingyuan and proclaiming that they would take Yan.

sentences.zh: 休哥聞之，先以兵扼其要地。

translations.literal: Xiuge heard of it and first sent troops to block the strategic places.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge heard of this and preemptively seized the key positions.

sentences.zh: 會太后軍至，接戰，殺敬源，廷讓走瀛州。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's army arrived they joined battle; Jingyuan was killed and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's army arrived they gave battle, killed Li Jingyuan, and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，宋遣劉廷讓等乘暑潦來攻易州，諸將憚之；

translations.literal: In the seventh year Song sent Liu Tingrang and others, taking advantage of summer floods to attack Yizhou; the generals were afraid of them;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Liu Tingrang and others exploited the summer floods to attack Yizhou, and the other generals were wary;

sentences.zh: 獨休哥率銳卒逆擊於沙河之北，殺傷數萬，獲輜重不可計，獻於朝。

translations.literal: only Xiuge alone led crack troops to meet the attack north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands, capturing baggage beyond reckoning, and presenting it at court.
translations.idiomatic: only Xiuge led crack troops to meet them north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands and capturing baggage beyond count, all of which he presented at court.

sentences.zh: 太后嘉其功，詔免拜、不名。

translations.literal: The empress dowager praised his merit and decreed exemption from bowing and from naming his name.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager praised his achievements and decreed that he need not bow when appearing and that his name was not to be spoken aloud in his presence.

sentences.zh: 自是宋不敢北向。

translations.literal: From this Song dared not turn northward.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Song dared not campaign northward.

sentences.zh: 時宋人欲止兒啼，乃曰：「於越至矣！」

translations.literal: At that time when Song people wished to stop a child crying they would say: "The Yuyue has come!"
translations.idiomatic: In Song, mothers hushed crying infants by saying, "The Yuyue is here!"

sentences.zh: 休哥以燕民疲弊，省賦役，恤孤寡，戒戍兵無犯宋境，雖馬牛逸於北者悉還之。

translations.literal: Xiuge, seeing the people of Yan worn out and impoverished, reduced taxes and corvée labor, cared for widows and orphans, and warned the garrison troops not to violate Song territory; even cattle and horses that strayed north were all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the people of Yan worn out and impoverished, Xiuge reduced taxes and corvée labor, cared for widows and orphans, and ordered the garrison not to violate Song territory; even cattle and horses that strayed north were all sent back.

sentences.zh: 遠近向化，邊鄙以安。

translations.literal: Near and far turned toward his rule, and the borderlands were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far submitted to his rule, and the borderlands were settled.

sentences.zh: 十六年，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 是夕，雨木冰。

translations.literal: That night rain froze on trees.
translations.idiomatic: That night rain froze on trees.

sentences.zh: 聖宗詔立祠南京。

translations.literal: Emperor Shengzong decreed that a shrine be established at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shengzong decreed that a shrine be established at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 休哥智略宏遠，料敵如神。

translations.literal: Xiuge's strategy was vast and far-reaching; he gauged the enemy like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge's plans were far-reaching and he read the enemy as if by divination.

sentences.zh: 每戰勝，讓功諸將，故士卒樂為之用。

translations.literal: Whenever he won battle he yielded merit to the generals, so the soldiers were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: After every victory he credited his fellow generals, and for that reason his men fought willingly for him.

sentences.zh: 身更百戰，未嘗殺一無辜。

translations.literal: He personally passed through a hundred battles and never once killed one innocent person.
translations.idiomatic: Through a hundred battles he never once killed an innocent man.

sentences.zh: 二子：高八，官至節度使；

translations.literal: Two sons: Gaoba, who reached the office of military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Gaoba, who rose to military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 高十，終於越。

translations.literal: Gaoshi, who ended as Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: and Gaoshi, who ended his career as Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 孫馬哥。

translations.literal: A grandson, Mage.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Mage.

translations.literal: 〈Supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Supplement〉

sentences.zh: 馬哥

translations.literal: Mage
translations.idiomatic: Mage

sentences.zh: 馬哥，字訛特懶。

translations.literal: Mage, courtesy name Wotelan.
translations.idiomatic: Mage, whose courtesy name was Wotelan.

sentences.zh: 興宗時，以散職入見，上問：「卿奉佛乎？」

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xingzong he entered audience in a minor post; the emperor asked: "Do you worship the Buddha?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xingzong he appeared at court in a minor post. The emperor asked, "Do you worship the Buddha?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣每旦誦太祖、太宗及先臣遺訓，未暇奉佛。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Each morning your servant recites the teachings left by Taizu, Taizong, and my forebear; I have no leisure to worship the Buddha."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my late forebear; I have had no time for Buddhism."

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 清寧中，遷唐古部節度使。

translations.literal: In Qingning he was transferred to military commissioner of the Tanggu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingning era he was made military commissioner of the Tanggu tribes.

sentences.zh: 咸雍中，累遷匡義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Xianyong he was repeatedly promoted to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xianyong era he rose in stages to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 大康初，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the start of Dakang he retired; he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dakang he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 耶律斜軫，字韓隱，於越曷魯之孫。

translations.literal: Yelu Xiezhen, courtesy name Hanyin, was a grandson of yuyue Helu.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiezhen, whose courtesy name was Hanyin, was a grandson of yuyue Helu.

sentences.zh: 性明敏，不事生產。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright and keen and did not engage in production.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright and quick-witted by nature and did not concern himself with farming or trade.

sentences.zh: 保寧元年，樞密使蕭思溫薦斜軫有經國才，上曰：「朕知之，第佚蕩，豈可羈屈？」

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoning, Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiao Siwen recommended Xiezhen as having talent to govern the state. The emperor said, "I know him—but he is unrestrained and dissolute; how can he be kept in harness?"
translations.idiomatic: In Baoning 1, Privy Council Commissioner Xiao Siwen recommended Xiezhen as possessing talent to govern the state. The emperor said, "I know him, but he is free-spirited and unruly—how can he be confined to office?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「外雖佚蕩，中未可量。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Outwardly he may seem unrestrained, but what lies within cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Though he appears unrestrained outwardly, what lies within cannot yet be judged."

sentences.zh: 乃召問以時政，占對剴切，帝器重之。

translations.literal: He was then summoned and questioned on current affairs; his answers were incisive and exact, and the emperor valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned and questioned on current affairs; his replies were sharp and apt, and the emperor came to esteem him highly.

sentences.zh: 妻以皇后之侄，命節制西南面諸軍，仍援河東。

translations.literal: He was given in marriage the empress's niece, ordered to take command of the armies of the Southwest, and still to support Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor married him to the empress's niece, appointed him to command the southwestern armies, and ordered him to reinforce Hedong.

sentences.zh: 改南院大王。

translations.literal: He was changed to Great King of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Great King of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初，宋再攻河東，從耶律沙至白馬嶺遇敵，沙等戰不利；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, when Song again attacked Hedong, he followed Yelu Sha to White Horse Ridge and met the enemy; Sha and the others fought without success;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianheng, when Song again attacked Hedong, he followed Yelu Sha to White Horse Ridge and encountered the enemy; Sha and the others were defeated;

sentences.zh: 斜軫赴之，令麾下萬矢齊發，敵氣褫而退。

translations.literal: Xiezhen hurried to them, ordered his troops to let ten thousand arrows fly together, and the enemy's spirit was cowed and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen hurried to the scene, ordered his men to unleash ten thousand arrows at once, and the enemy lost heart and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，宋下河東，乘勝襲燕，北院大王耶律奚底與蕭討古逆戰，敗績，退屯清河北。

translations.literal: That autumn Song descended on Hedong and, riding their victory, raided Yan; Great King of the Northern Court Yelu Xidi and Xiao Taogu met them in battle, suffered defeat, and withdrew to encamp north of the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Song overran Hedong and, pressing their advantage, struck at Yan; Great King of the Northern Court Yelu Xidi and Xiao Taogu met them in battle, were routed, and fell back to encamp north of the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 斜軫取奚底等青幟軍於得勝口以誘敵，敵果爭赴。

translations.literal: Xiezhen took Xidi's green-banner army at Desheng Pass to lure the enemy, and the enemy indeed rushed to engage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen took Xidi's green-banner force at Desheng Pass to lure the enemy, and the enemy rushed to meet them as expected.

sentences.zh: 斜軫出其後，奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Xiezhen came out behind them and struck hard, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen struck from behind and routed them.

sentences.zh: 及高梁之戰，與耶律休哥分左右翼夾擊，大敗宋軍。

translations.literal: At the battle of Gaoliang he and Yelu Xiuge took left and right wings in a pincer attack and inflicted a great defeat on the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Gaoliang he and Yelu Xiuge took the left and right wings in a pincer attack and routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 統和初，皇太后稱制，益見委任，為北院樞密使。

translations.literal: At the start of Tonghe the empress dowager held regency; he was increasingly entrusted and made Commissioner of the Northern Court Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tonghe, when the empress dowager assumed regency, he was increasingly trusted and made Commissioner of the Northern Court Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 會宋將曹彬、米信出雄、易，楊繼業出代州。

translations.literal: It happened that Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin came out from Xiong and Yi, and Yang Ye from Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin advanced from Xiong and Yi, Yang Ye marched out from Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 太后親帥師救燕，以斜軫為山西路兵馬都統。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally led the army to rescue Yan and made Xiezhen overall commander of Shanxi Route military forces.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager led the army in person to relieve Yan and appointed Xiezhen overall commander of the Shanxi Route forces.

sentences.zh: 繼業陷山西諸郡，各以兵守，自屯代州。

translations.literal: Ye overran the commanderies of Shanxi, each garrisoned with troops; he himself encamped at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had overrun the Shanxi commanderies and left troops to hold each; he himself encamped at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 斜軫至定安，遇賀令圖軍，擊破之，追至五臺，斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Xiezhen reached Ding'an, met He Lingtu's army, defeated it, pursued to Wutai, and took heads numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen reached Ding'an, met He Lingtu's army, routed it, and pursued to Wutai, taking tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 明日，至蔚州，敵不敢出，斜軫書帛射城上，諭以招慰意。

translations.literal: The next day he reached Weizhou; the enemy dared not come out; Xiezhen wrote on silk, shot it onto the wall, and instructed them with words of recruitment and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reached Weizhou. The enemy would not sally forth, so Xiezhen shot a message written on silk onto the walls offering terms of surrender and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 陰聞宋軍來救，令都監耶律題子夜伏兵險厄，俟敵至而發。

translations.literal: Secretly hearing Song troops were coming to the relief, he ordered the commandant Yelu Tizi to lie in ambush by night in a narrow pass and strike when the enemy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Learning secretly that Song relief was coming, he ordered Commandant Yelu Tizi to lay an ambush by night in a defile and strike when the enemy arrived.

sentences.zh: 城守者見救至，突出。

translations.literal: The city defenders, seeing relief had come, sallied forth.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison, seeing relief had arrived, burst out of the city.

sentences.zh: 斜軫擊其背，二軍俱潰，追至飛狐，斬首二萬餘級，遂取蔚州。

translations.literal: Xiezhen struck their rear; both armies were routed; pursuit reached Feihu; more than twenty thousand heads were taken; thus Weizhou was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen struck them from behind; both Song forces broke; he pursued to Feihu, took more than twenty thousand heads, and captured Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 賀令圖、潘美復以兵來，斜軫逆於飛狐，擊敗之。

translations.literal: He Lingtu and Pan Mei came again with troops; Xiezhen met them at Feihu and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He Lingtu and Pan Mei returned with troops; Xiezhen met them at Feihu and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 宋軍在渾源、應州者，皆棄城走。

translations.literal: Song troops at Hunyuan and Yingzhou all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song garrisons at Hunyuan and Yingzhou all abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 斜軫聞繼業出兵，令蕭撻凜伏兵於路。

translations.literal: Xiezhen heard Ye was marching out and ordered Xiao Tadin to lie in ambush along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiezhen heard that Ye was marching out, he ordered Xiao Tadin to set an ambush along the road.

sentences.zh: 明旦，繼業兵至，斜軫擁眾為戰勢。

translations.literal: At dawn Ye's troops arrived; Xiezhen massed his force in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Ye's army arrived, and Xiezhen drew up his troops for battle.

sentences.zh: 繼業麾幟而前，斜軫佯退。

translations.literal: Ye advanced with banners waving; Xiezhen feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Ye advanced under his banners; Xiezhen feigned a retreat.

sentences.zh: 伏兵發，斜軫進攻，繼業敗走，至狼牙村，眾軍皆潰。

translations.literal: The ambush was sprung; Xiezhen pressed the attack; Ye was defeated and fled; reaching Langya Village, the whole army scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang up and Xiezhen pressed the attack. Ye was routed and fled to Langya Village, where his whole army broke apart.

sentences.zh: 繼業為流矢所中，被擒。

translations.literal: Ye was struck by a stray arrow and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was struck by a stray arrow and taken captive.

sentences.zh: 斜軫責曰：「汝與我國角勝三十餘年，今日何面目相見！」

translations.literal: Xiezhen rebuked him, saying: "You have contested victory with our state for more than thirty years—what face have you to meet me today!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen reproached him: "You have fought our state for more than thirty years—what face do you bring to this meeting!"

sentences.zh: 繼業但稱死罪而已。

translations.literal: Ye could only speak of his capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye could only plead for death.

sentences.zh: 初，繼業在宋以驍勇聞，人號楊無敵，首建梗邊之策。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ye in Song was known for fierce valor; men called him Yang the Invincible; he was the first to propose obstructing the border.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Song service Yang Ye had been famed for valor; people called him Yang the Invincible, and he had been first to urge a hard line on the border.

sentences.zh: 至狼牙村，心惡之，欲避不可得。

translations.literal: When they reached Langya Village, his heart hated the omen; he wished to avoid it but could not.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Langya Village he dreaded the name, wished to avoid the place, and could not.

sentences.zh: 既擒，三日死。

translations.literal: Once captured, within three days he died.
translations.idiomatic: After his capture he died within three days.

sentences.zh: 斜軫歸闕，以功加守太保。

translations.literal: Xiezhen returned to court; for his merit he was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen returned to court and, for his achievements, was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 從太后南伐，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Following the empress dowager on the southern campaign, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's southern campaign he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 太后親為哀臨，仍給葬具。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally mourned him and also supplied funeral goods.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager mourned him in person and provided funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 庶子狗兒，官至小將軍。

translations.literal: A secondary son, Gou'er, reached the office of junior general.
translations.idiomatic: A son by a concubine, Gou'er, rose to junior general.

sentences.zh: 耶律奚低

translations.literal: Yelu Xidi
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xidi

sentences.zh: 耶律奚低，孟父楚國王之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，勇於攻戰。

translations.literal: Skilled with bow and horse, bold in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled with bow and horse and bold in attack.

sentences.zh: 景宗時，多任以軍事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jingzong's time he was often entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jingzong he was often entrusted with military command.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，為右皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe he was Right Pishi Xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe he became Right Pishi Xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 時宋將楊繼業陷山西郡縣，奚低從樞密使斜軫討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Song general Yang Ye overran the commanderies and counties of Shanxi; Xidi followed the Privy Council commissioner Xiezhen to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Yang Ye overran the Shanxi commanderies, Xidi followed Privy Council Commissioner Xiezhen against him.

sentences.zh: 凡戰必以身先，矢無虛發。

translations.literal: In every battle he must take the lead in person; no arrow went without its mark.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led from the front, and never wasted an arrow.

sentences.zh: 繼業敗於朔州之南，匿深林中。

translations.literal: Ye was defeated south of Shuozhou and hid in a deep forest.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was defeated south of Shuozhou and hid in deep forest.

sentences.zh: 奚低望袍影而射，繼業墮馬。

translations.literal: Xidi, sighting the shadow of a robe, shot; Ye fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Xidi caught sight of a robe's shadow and shot; Ye fell from his horse.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍令須生擒繼業，奚低以故不能為功。

translations.literal: Earlier, army orders required Ye to be captured alive; for this reason Xidi could not claim the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier orders had required Ye to be taken alive, so for that reason Xidi could not claim the credit.

sentences.zh: 後太后南伐，屢有戰績。

translations.literal: Later on the empress dowager's southern campaign he repeatedly had battle achievements.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's later southern campaigns he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 以病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 耶律學古

translations.literal: Yelu Xuegu
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xuegu

sentences.zh: 耶律學古，字乙辛隱，於越窪之庶孫。

translations.literal: Yelu Xuegu, courtesy name Yixin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xuegu, whose courtesy name was Yixinyin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.

sentences.zh: 穎悟好學，工譯鞮及詩。

translations.literal: Clever and fond of learning, skilled at translating Di language and at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and studious, he was skilled at translating the Di tongue and at poetry.

sentences.zh: 保寧中，補禦盞郎君。

translations.literal: In Baoning he was appointed Cupbearer of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoning he was appointed cupbearer of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 乾亨元年，宋既下河東，乘勝侵燕，學古受詔往援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianheng, after Song had taken Hedong and pressed the advantage to invade Yan, Xuegu received orders to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianheng, after Song had taken Hedong and pressed on into Yan, Xuegu was ordered to the relief.

sentences.zh: 始至京，宋敗耶律奚底、蕭討古等，勢益張，圍城三周，穴地而進，城中民懷二心。

translations.literal: When he first reached the capital, Song had already defeated Yelu Xidi, Xiao Taogu, and others; their momentum grew; they besieged the city for three circuits, advanced by tunneling underground, and the people in the city wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached the capital, Song had already defeated Yelu Xidi, Xiao Taogu, and others. Their momentum swelled; they besieged the city on three sides, tunneled underground to advance, and the townspeople wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 學古以計安反側，隨宜備禦，晝夜不少懈。

translations.literal: Xuegu by stratagem settled the wavering, prepared defense as each situation required, and never relaxed day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Xuegu by stratagem reassured the wavering, made defenses as each situation required, and never slackened day or night.

sentences.zh: 適有敵三百餘人夜登城，學古戰卻之。

translations.literal: It happened that more than three hundred enemies climbed the wall by night; Xuegu fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: When more than three hundred enemy troops climbed the walls by night, Xuegu fought them off.

sentences.zh: 會援軍至，圍遂解。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When relief arrived the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 學古開門列陣，四面鳴鼓，居民大呼，聲震天地。

translations.literal: Xuegu opened the gates and formed ranks; drums sounded on four sides; residents shouted aloud; the sound shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Xuegu opened the gates and drew up his ranks; drums sounded on every side and the townspeople shouted until the noise shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 旋有高梁之捷。

translations.literal: Soon came the victory at Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon came the victory at Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 以功遙授保靜軍節度使，為南京馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given in absentia the post of military commissioner of Baojing Army and made overall commander of cavalry and infantry of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given in absentia the post of military commissioner of the Baojing Army and made overall commander of the Southern Capital's cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 二年，伐宋，乞將漢軍，從之，改彰國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the campaign against Song, he begged to command Han troops and was granted it; he was changed to military commissioner of Zhangguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the campaign against Song, he asked to command Han troops and was granted this; he was made military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army.

sentences.zh: 時南境未靜，民思休息，學古禁寇掠以安之。

translations.literal: At that time the southern border was not yet settled and the people longed for rest; Xuegu forbade raiding and plunder to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The southern border was not yet quiet and the people longed for peace; Xuegu forbade raiding and plunder to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 會宋將潘美率兵分道來侵，學古以軍少，虛張旗幟，雜丁黃為疑兵。

translations.literal: When Song general Pan Mei led troops by several routes to invade, Xuegu's army was few; he falsely displayed many banners and mixed old and young as dummy troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Pan Mei invaded by several routes, Xuegu's force was small; he displayed many banners and mixed men and boys as dummy troops.

sentences.zh: 是夜，適獨虎峪舉烽火，遣人偵視，見敵俘掠村野，擊之，悉獲所掠物，擒其將領。

translations.literal: That night, by chance a beacon was lit at Duhu Valley; he sent men to reconnoiter, saw the enemy plundering villages and fields, attacked them, recovered all looted goods, and captured their officers.
translations.idiomatic: That night a beacon happened to be raised at Duhu Valley; he sent scouts, found the enemy plundering villages, attacked them, recovered all that had been taken, and captured their officers.

sentences.zh: 自是學古與潘美各守邊約，無相侵軼，民獲安業。

translations.literal: From this Xuegu and Pan Mei each kept border truce and did not encroach on one another; the people were able to live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xuegu and Pan Mei each kept the border pact and did not encroach on one another, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 以功為惕隱，卒。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made Tiyi; he died.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Tiyi; he died.

sentences.zh: 弟烏不呂。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wubulü.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Wubulü.

translations.literal: 〈Supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Supplement〉

sentences.zh: 烏不呂

translations.literal: Wubulü
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü

sentences.zh: 烏不呂，字留隱。

translations.literal: Wubulü, courtesy name Liuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü, whose courtesy name was Liuyin.

sentences.zh: 嚴重，有膂力，善屬文。

translations.literal: Stern and dignified, with muscular strength, skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and imposing, powerfully built, and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 統和中伐宋，屢任以軍事。

translations.literal: On the Tonghe campaign against Song he was repeatedly entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe campaigns against Song he was repeatedly entrusted with military command.

sentences.zh: 嘗與爻直不相能，因曰：「爾奴才，何所知？」

translations.literal: He once did not get along with Yaozhi and therefore said: "You slave—what do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled with Yaozhi and said, "You slave—what do you know?"

sentences.zh: 爻直訟於北院樞密使韓德讓。

translations.literal: Yaozhi sued him at Northern Court Privy Council Commissioner Han Derang.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi brought suit before Northern Court Privy Council Commissioner Han Derang.

sentences.zh: 德讓怒，問曰：「爾安得此奴耶？」

translations.literal: Derang was angry and asked: "How did you come by such a slave?"
translations.idiomatic: Derang was angry and asked, "How did you come by such a slave?"

sentences.zh: 烏不呂對曰：「三父異籍時亦易得。」

translations.literal: Wubulü replied: "In the days of the three fathers with different registers they were easy to obtain too."
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü answered, "In the days when the three fathers kept separate registers they were easy to come by too."

sentences.zh: 德讓笑而釋之。

translations.literal: Derang laughed and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Derang laughed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 後從蕭恒德伐蒲盧毛朵部，以功為東路統軍都監。

translations.literal: Later he followed Xiao Hengde against the Pulumao Duo tribe; for merit he was made eastern route army overall commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Xiao Hengde against the Pulumao Duo tribe and, for his merit, was made eastern-route army overall commandant.

sentences.zh: 及德讓為大丞相，薦其材可任統軍使，太后曰：「烏不呂嘗不遜於卿，何善而薦？」

translations.literal: When Derang became Grand Chancellor he recommended him as fit for army commander; the empress dowager said: "Wubulü was once disrespectful to you—why recommend him with praise?"
translations.idiomatic: When Derang became Grand Chancellor he recommended Wubulü as fit to be an army commander. The empress dowager said, "Wubulü was once disrespectful to you—why do you praise him now?"

sentences.zh: 德讓奏曰：「臣忝相位，於臣猶不屈，況於其餘。

translations.literal: Derang submitted: "Your servant has humbly held the chief ministership; before me he would not yield—how much more before others.
translations.idiomatic: Derang replied, "I have humbly held the chief ministership, yet he would not yield even to me—how much more to others.

sentences.zh: 以此知可用。

translations.literal: From this I know he can be used.
translations.idiomatic: From this I know he can be used.

sentences.zh: 若任使之，必能鎮撫諸蕃。」

translations.literal: If employed, he will surely be able to pacify the various tribes."
translations.idiomatic: If he is employed, he will surely be able to pacify the frontier tribes."

sentences.zh: 太后從之，加金紫崇祿大夫、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 而弟國留以罪亡，烏不呂及其母俱下吏。

translations.literal: But his younger brother Guoliu fled because of a crime; Wubulü and his mother were both put in the hands of officials.
translations.idiomatic: But his younger brother Guoliu fled after committing a crime, and Wubulü and his mother were both handed over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 恐禍及母，陰使人召國留，紿曰：「太后知事之誣，汝第來勿畏。」

translations.literal: Fearing disaster would reach his mother, he secretly sent men to summon Guoliu, deceiving him: "The empress dowager knows the matter was false—you come alone and need not fear."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing harm would reach his mother, he secretly sent men to summon Guoliu, telling him, "The empress dowager knows the charge is false—come alone and have no fear."

sentences.zh: 國留至，送有司，坐誅。

translations.literal: Guoliu arrived and was handed to the authorities; he was punished by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliu came, was handed to the authorities, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 其後，退歸田里，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Afterward he retired to his village home and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he retired to his home village and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋乘下太原之銳，以師圍燕，繼遣曹彬、楊繼業等分道來伐。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Song, riding the sharp edge of having taken Taiyuan, used their army to besiege Yan, and then sent Cao Bin, Yang Ye, and others by separate routes to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Song, riding the momentum of taking Taiyuan, besieged Yan with their army and then sent Cao Bin, Yang Ye, and others to attack by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 是兩役也，遼亦岌岌乎殆哉！

translations.literal: In these two campaigns Liao was also in peril indeed!
translations.idiomatic: In these two campaigns Liao was brought to the brink indeed!

sentences.zh: 休哥奮擊於高梁，敵兵奔潰；

translations.literal: Xiuge struck fiercely at Gaoliang and the enemy army fled in rout;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge struck hard at Gaoliang and the enemy broke and fled;

sentences.zh: 斜軫擒繼業於朔州，旋復故地。

translations.literal: Xiezhen captured Ye at Shuo and soon recovered the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen captured Yang Ye at Shuo and soon recovered the lost territory.

sentences.zh: 宋自是不復深入，社稷固而邊境寧，雖配古名將，無愧矣。

translations.literal: Song from this did not again penetrate deeply; the altars were secure and the borderlands peaceful—though matched with famous generals of antiquity, they need not blush.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Song did not penetrate deeply again; the altars were secure and the borders quiet—matched against famous generals of old, they need not blush.

sentences.zh: 然非學古之在南京安其反側，則二將之功，蓋亦難致。

translations.literal: Yet had it not been for Xuegu at the Southern Capital settling the wavering, the merit of the two generals would probably have been hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet had Xuegu not settled the wavering hearts at the Southern Capital, the achievements of the two generals would probably have been hard to win.

sentences.zh: 故曰國以人重，信哉！

translations.literal: Therefore it is said a state is weighty because of its men—true indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said that a state is made weighty by its men—how true!
